correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the n-coordinate zero-sum sphere with n-2-dimensional tangent chart at every balanced two-level minimum. The exact width identity, sphere Jacobian and positive coercive maximum gauge yield the uniform tangent-polytope limit in total variation. Euclidean volume of each one-block max-gauge simplex is sqrt(p)*p^(p-1)*s^(p-1)/(p-1)!, and convolution gives p^(p-1/2)q^(q-1/2)/(n-2)!, including singleton blocks. Multiplying by the exact number of minima, chart scale and sphere normalization yields C_n with n=3,4,5 checks. The sharpened upper/lower local slope extrema have explicit equality configurations. Exact triangle and nonlinear tetrahedron checks in verify.py passed; numerical tests are not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The classical minimum-width equality problem leaves open the quantitative geometric structure of the rare orientations that nearly attain it. The all-dimensional total-variation tangent-polytope classification, exact spherical rare-event rate, conditional Dirichlet splitting and sharp angular condition numbers supply a motivated geometric stability/probability law rather than a routine restatement of a width bound. It distinguishes the full orientation geometry from the historically studied one-dimensional internally studentized range.
